about.text: Milk heated briefly to kill the bacteria that make people ill and spoil it, usually to about 72 °C for 15 seconds, and cooled again at once. It is named after Louis Pasteur, who showed in the 1860s that gentle heating kept wine and beer from souring.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

facts.v: EU: at least 72 °C for 15 s, or at least 63 °C for 30 min. US: 161 °F (72 °C) for 15 s, or 145 °F (63 °C) for 30 min
Usually 72–75 °C for 15–20 s for homogenised milk
The alkaline phosphatase test must come out negative
Low-temperature pasteurised milk (63 °C for 30 minutes) is a niche there, as most market milk is UHT
